blocks.text: This chapter stages a public conflict between two men identified as prophets. Hananiah promises a swift end to Babylon’s yoke, while Jeremiah does not treat that claim—or his own role—as self-authenticating. He points to whether a prophecy of peace comes to pass, and the narrative concludes by reporting Hananiah’s death that same year. The shifts among narration, competing prophetic speeches, and divine speech keep the question of authority before the reader: prophetic claims are tested by their outcome.
